newsitem.title: USA: Most U.S. debt futures close slightly lower.
newsitem.headline: Most U.S. debt futures close slightly lower.

text.p: U.S. debt futures closed mostly lower, but March T-bonds recouped losses that were set after the 10-year note auction results.
March T-bonds fell to 112-05/32, through support at 112-08/32 and 112-06/32, due to weak demand at the auction, traders and analysts said.
Although the average yield was on the low side of trade estimates at 6.37 percent, the bid-to-cover ratio was at 1.90.
"I thought the bid-to-cover was pretty disapppointing," one bond futures trader said.
Trading turned moderately active on the results.
Activity into the close, however, consisted of light position-squaring ahead of the U.S. January retail sales report.

U.S. January retail sales, which will be released at 0830 EST/1330 GMT on Thursday, are expected to rise 0.7 percent, from up 0.6 percent in December, and sales, excluding autos, are forecast to increase 0.6 percent, from up 0.6 percent in December.
Even if the data is lower than expected, traders and analysts said the upside will once again be limited ahead of the Treasury's 30-year bond auction.
While traders noted a solid underlying bid to the market, they said uncertainty ahead of retail sales and Friday's Producer Price Index (PPI), coupled with supply concerns, weighed on the market.
Some traders still look for March T-bonds to test 111-20/32 before re-testing 113-00, the one-month high set on Friday, February 7.
"You would expect some knee-jerk reaction to the auction, but I think this will set the stage for a move higher," one bond market analyst said.

He said good demand should emerge at Thursday's $10 billion 30-year bond auction, particularly from mortgage-backed dealers and funds shifting profits out of equities and into the fixed-income market.
Another analyst noted that U.S. bond futures appeared to be following the Standard & Poor's 500 futures market.
March T-bonds rose to 112-24/32 moments after March S&Ps soared through the key psychological resistance level of 800.00.
"If S&Ps have a strong close, look for an upside break-out in bonds," he said.

At the end of pit trade, March T-bonds were off 02/32 at 112-13/32, 10-year notes were off 01/32 at 109-15/32, June Eurodollars were steady at 94.35, September Eurodollars were down one basis point at 94.21, June T-bills were steady at 94.89, and March munibonds were up 04/32 at 116-08/32.
